analysis:
Examined ProviderLoop.swift head lines 1-1202; the only change is new stored state at lines 801-810: coordinatorConnection (DaemonState.CoordinatorConnection, reported to status/doctor), and unauthorized-recovery bookkeeping (unauthorizedSince, lastUnauthorizedReconnectAt, unauthorizedReconnectAttempts, a random jitter from UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.thresholdJitter) used by ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery (not supplied). DaemonState+Coding.swift adds a coordinatorConnection CodingKey (head line 18) and decode/encode lines (head 51, 90) via decodeIfPresent/encodeIfPresent, making decoding backward compatible with older state files.

No regression is identified in this batch. These are declarations and serialization only. Integration still needs to check the following.
(1) The CoordinatorConnection struct fields, which are not supplied. They must not persist provider API tokens (A-008), connection nonces, grant material (A-016) or stable identities that would raise T-058 linkage concerns in the daemon state file. The state file's owner-only permissions should also be confirmed.
(2) The ServingAuthorizationRecovery logic, which is not supplied. An adversarial coordinator response or a not-routable verdict that triggers a reconnect must be bounded by attempts and jitter so it cannot cause a reconnect storm (availability, A-018/T-057). The reconnect must not reuse stale authorization across connections (T-053), and must re-run full proof rather than extend Apple proof lifetime (TB-011).
(3) The writer of coordinatorConnection in writeDaemonState. Any local status consumer must treat it as diagnostic only, never as authorization (T-052).

The remaining ProviderLoop content (SendHandle, keypair generation, attestation signer) is unchanged.
